cim: Source: Trump dialed into Nvidia's board meeting to argue for Huang's return; a US official says he "was totally involved" and "we have to protect our geniuses" (Semafor)
cim_eredeti: Source: Trump dialed into Nvidia's board meeting to argue for Huang's return; a US official says he "was totally involved" and "we have to protect our geniuses" (Semafor)
szoveg_eredeti:
US President Donald Trump had dialed into Nvidia’s board meeting to argue for Jensen Huang’s return, hours before the company reinstated the ousted CEO, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Huang, saying the company had received assurances from “senior levels of the United States government” that he posed no national security risk after carrying on an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

“President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said.

Nvidia’s board met late last night, according to a person familiar with the matter, and voted unanimously. Huang’s resignation spurred an outcry from some Silicon Valley figures who called for his return. Semafor had previously reported that a faction of directors had continued to push for him to come back.

The anti-Jensen camp was dealt a blow when they learned a leading Huang replacement candidate, Arm CEO Rene Haas, had signed a new contract with Arm extending his employment until 2033, according to another person familiar with some directors’ thinking.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Harvey Jones, who was elevated at the time of Huang’s Nov. 12 ouster to board chairman, said in a statement.

The decision comes less than two weeks after Huang stepped down under pressure, and returns Huang to the company he founded in 1993 and built into an AI giant. Huang has also been accused of having an affair with a subordinate.

Nvidia’s stock was up nearly 30% in early trading Monday, the biggest jump in more than two decades.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., the ranking member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, called the decision to reinstate Huang “reckless.” Huang’s return “only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk,” she wrote.

— Ashley Gold and J.D. Capelouto contributed reporting.
